Article Title: Over 37 lakh appeals pending after Bengal SIR: EC tells Supreme Court
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Friday told the Supreme Court that over 37 lakh appeals against the deletion or inclusion of names in West Bengal electoral rolls under the Special Intensive Revision remain pending.The poll panel told the apex court in its response affidavit that tribunals appointed by the court have disposed of only about 1.02 lakh of the 38.20 lakh appeals filed so far.This comes after a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymala Bagchi and V Mohana sought the poll panel's response to a plea seeking disclosure of assembly constituency-wise data on claims and objections filed by voters whose names were deleted during the SIR exercise.A total of 38,20,683 appeals had been filed against orders relating to the SIR of electoral rolls. Of these, 1,02,231 appeals had been disposed of, leaving 37,18,452 pending, the poll panel said.The affidavit, however, did not provide a break-up of the appeals filed by electors whose names were deleted and those filed against the inclusion of names in the electoral rolls.Prasenjit Bose, who filed the affidavit, claimed that more than 58 lakh electors were excluded during the enumeration phase of the SIR exercise in West Bengal.He added that while 9.64 lakh applications for inclusion (Forms 6 and 6A) and over 99,000 applications for deletion (Form 7) were received during the claims and objections phase, only around 1.82 lakh additions were reflected in the final electoral roll published on February 28.On August 25, the top court directed the Election Commission to submit data on the pendency and disposal of appeals before tribunals challenging exclusion or inclusion in electoral rolls.Observing that these appeals needed to be adjudicated in a time-bound manner, the bench had asked the poll panel to explain what steps were being taken to streamline the mechanism for disposing of pending appeals and how many additional tribunals were required.The EC data submitted to the court showed that 34.13 lakh Form 6 applications had been filed between December 17, 2025, when the draft electoral roll was published, and August 7, 2026.Form 6 is the statutory application for inclusion of a name in the electoral roll.On April 24, the apex court asked the appellate tribunals to give out-of-turn hearings to those who made a case for urgent hearing against deletion from electoral rolls after the SIR.Approximately 700 judicial officers from West Bengal and neighbouring Odisha and Jharkhand were deployed to deal with around 60 lakh claims and objections.Later, the chief justice of the Calcutta high court, on the direction of the top court, set up 19 tribunals headed by former high court chief justices and judges to decide the appeals.
Article Summary: Election commission tells supreme court that over 37 lakh appeals against the deletion or inclusion of names in west bengal electoral rolls remain pending. This comes after a bench of chief justice surya kant and justices joymala bagchi and v mohana sought the poll panel's response.

Article Title: "Process being carried out in accordance with prescribed rules": Uttarakhand Govt on proposed procurement of 1320 MW of thermal power
Article Text:
"Process being carried out in accordance with prescribed rules": Uttarakhand Govt on proposed procurement of 1320 MW of thermal power

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

UTTARAKHAND: Uttarakhand Principal Secretary (Energy) R Meenakshi Sundaram on Thursday issued a clarification on questions raised by some political parties over the proposed procurement of 1,320 MW of thermal power, saying the process is being carried out in accordance with prescribed rules, technical requirements, competitive bidding and approval from the Uttarakhand Electricity Regulatory Commission (UERC).Sundaram said allegations regarding the power procurement process were not based on facts and that the objective was to secure the state's long-term and growing electricity requirements, rather than benefit any particular company.Clarifying the tender process, he said the Model Bidding Document issued by the Union Power Ministry in 2019 was a general model document and that changes were examined based on the technology, location, fuel availability, transportation costs and other circumstances of individual projects.He said suggestions and objections received from bidders during the tender process were examined from technical and practical perspectives, following which necessary proposed changes were placed before UERC.The Commission approved the amendments after detailed deliberations.Sundaram also rejected the perception that power procurement was being awarded to a particular company without competition. He said five companies were found eligible at the Request for Quotation (RFQ) stage and competition had also been maintained during the Request for Proposal (RFP) stage."The final selection will be based on the total tariff quoted through the competitive bidding process," he said.The Principal Secretary said the proposed 1,320 MW procurement was aimed at meeting Uttarakhand's long-term baseload requirement and ensuring continuous and reliable power supply to consumers.He said Uttarakhand's importance as a tourism and pilgrimage destination, along with its environmental sensitivity, had been considered while framing the tender. Since thermal power plants require large quantities of coal, transporting it over long distances could increase costs.The tender therefore allows the plant to be established at any suitable location in the country, enabling companies to quote competitive tariffs after considering fuel availability, transportation costs and other factors.Sundaram clarified that there was no restriction on setting up the plant in Uttarakhand and that any company establishing a plant in the state and offering electricity at a competitive tariff could participate in the prescribed process.On transmission costs, he said the arrangements and associated expenses for supplying electricity to Uttarakhand would be determined according to the tender and tariff conditions. "Therefore, the claim that establishing the plant outside Uttarakhand would automatically result in the entire additional cost being borne by consumers was not correct."He said the actual financial impact on consumers would have to be assessed on the basis of the total electricity tariff.On fixed charges, Sundaram said the Model Bidding Document prescribed a fixed charge ceiling of 70 per cent, with at least 30 per cent remaining as fuel charge. Considering bidders' actual costs, fuel availability and circumstances of potential locations, UPCL proposed increasing the fixed charge ceiling to 75 per cent, allowing the fuel charge component to be kept at up to 25 per cent.He said electricity prices were not evaluated solely on the basis of fixed charges but on the total tariff comprising fixed charges and variable or fuel costs. The proposal was examined and approved by UERC after due deliberation.Sundaram said an increase in the fixed charge ceiling from 70 per cent to 75 per cent did not automatically mean an additional financial burden on consumers, as the final payment would depend on the total tariff quoted through competitive bidding.He said construction timelines had also been prescribed to make the 1,320 MW capacity available in phases, with 42 months prescribed for the first unit and 48 months for the second unit.The Principal Secretary said the option of a joint venture between UJVNL and THDC was also considered to meet the requirement. "However, THDC, a subsidiary of NTPC, is required to follow NTPC's prescribed policies, while its core expertise is in hydropower and Pumped Storage Projects. Expansion into other areas would require necessary approvals from its promoter."Sundaram also clarified that the estimated figure of Rs 1.60 lakh crore to Rs 1.66 lakh crore over 25 years did not represent a one-time payment but the potential total payment over the entire period.He said the state's future power requirement had been assessed on the basis of the Central Electricity Authority's Resource Adequacy Study and that actual payments would depend on the final tariff, power supplied, plant availability and other contractual conditions.Reiterating that the procurement process was not a departmental decision alone, Sundaram said it involved multiple stages, including technical examination, bidder competition, financial evaluation and approval by an independent regulatory authority.He reiterated that the primary objective of procuring 1,320 MW was to secure Uttarakhand's future electricity requirements and not to benefit any particular company. The final selection, he said, would be made through competitive bidding.
Article Summary: "process being carried out in accordance with prescribed rules": uttarakhand govt on proposed procurement of 1320 mw of thermal power. Sundaram said allegations regarding the power procurement process were not based on facts and that the objective was to secure the state's long-term and growing electricity requirements.

Article Title: 'BJP and EC join forces to split party': Rahul Gandhi slams EC over TMC name, symbol freeze
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Friday slammed the Election Commission for barring TMC from using party name and symbol in the upcoming assembly bypolls in West Bengal, accusing the poll panel and Bharatiya Janata Party of joining forces to split a party.In a social media post on X, Rahul pointed towards the past examples of split in shiv Sena and NCP."First Shiv Sena, then NCP, and now Trinamool Congress . Every time, the same pattern—BJP and the Election Commission join forces to split a party. Then its election symbol is snatched away," the Congress leader said."When an entire party can be stolen, it's hardly surprising that the votes of millions of Indians can be stolen too," he added.Rahul also said that "vote chori, sarkaar chori and now party chori have become the symbols of democratic decline" in the country."Vote theft. Government theft. Now party theft—these have become symbols of our democratic decline. The ECI's constitutional responsibility is to protect the mandate—but instead, it's aiding those very forces that overturn the people's verdict," the Congress leader said."This fight isn't just Mamata Banerjee's. It's the fight of every political party, every voter who wants free and fair elections," he added.Rahul's remarks came after the poll panel, in its interim order, ruled that neither faction of TMC can use its name or "flowers and grass" symbol after acknowledging a split between factions led by Mamata Banerjee and Arup Roy.Both groups will have to contest the bypolls under different names and with election symbols allotted by the Commission. This arrangement will continue until the dispute is finally settled.EC said two rival groups each claimed to be the "real" party, requiring substantive determination under Paragraph 15 of the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968. It said the interim measure, based on precedents, would place them on an "even keel".Meanwhile, West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh claimed that TMC is crumbling under the weight of severe internal strife following the Election Commission's interim order."The Trinamool Congress (TMC) is disintegrating due to internal infighting. The public has rejected them. Their MPs are in other parties, and Mamata Banerjee stands alone. They hold no documents regarding this; the Election Commission will make the decision," he said.The poll panel has been hearing competing claims from the two factions over control of the party, its name and election symbol. Both sides have submitted documents and appeared before the Commission during the proceedings.The dispute reached the Election Commission in July after the rival factions staked competing claims to control of the TMC. The panel subsequently sought responses on issues including organisational control, authorised signatories, party assets, name and election symbol.
Article Summary: Lok sabha leader of opposition rahul gandhi slams the election commission for barring tmc from using party name and symbol in west bengal bypolls. He accuses the poll panel and bharatiya janata party of joining forces to split a party. Rahul also said that "vote chori, sarkaar chori and now party chori have become the symbols of democratic decline"

Article Title: ‘Umar Khalid is a nationalist’: B K Hariprasad’s remark sparks BJP attack
Article Text:
Karnataka Congress president B K Hariprasad called jailed activist Umar Khalid a nationalist.





BENGALURU: Karnataka Congress president B K Hariprasad Tuesday called jailed activist Umar Khalid a “nationalist” and criticised Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad ( ABVP ) for opposing a proposed screening of a documentary on him at National Law School of India University (NLSIU).“ABVP has no right to speak about Khalid because ABVP adores Nathuram Godse, who is anti-national and the first terrorist of the country,” Hariprasad said.The remarks came after ABVP in Bengaluru demanded cancellation of the proposed screening of filmmaker Lalit Vachani’s documentary, ‘Prisoner No. 626710 is Present’, at NLSIU. The documentary was scheduled to be screened Monday by the law and society committee, a student organisation at the university. NLSIU later said it had to reschedule the event due to “logistical and security considerations”.The screening was to express solidarity with Khalid and to mark six years since his imprisonment without trial under Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act in connection with the 2020 Delhi riots.BJP hit back at Hariprasad’s remarks, calling them deeply condemnable. In New Delhi, Sambit Patra, MP, linked Hariprasad’s remarks to Congress’ past interactions with Kashmiri separatist leader Yasin Malik.“Just think about it: this is the same Umar Khalid,” Patra said. “During the Citizenship Amendment Act protests in Feb 2020, so many people were killed in Delhi. A case was filed under UAPA. The matter was heard across multiple courts; even in Feb 2026, the Supreme Court rejected Umar Khalid’s bail plea. Look at the sympathy Congress party harbours for the very same Umar Khalid.”Patra also attacked Congress party over its meetings with Yasin Malik, alleging the party had reduced itself to “appeasement”.
Article Summary: Karnataka congress president b k hariprasad called jailed activist umar khalid a nationalist. He criticised akhil bharatiya vidyarthi parishad ( abvp ) for opposing a proposed screening of a documentary on him at national law school of india university.

Article Title: 'It can't be that Hindi will not be taught in Tamil Nadu', SC tells state during hearing on Navodaya schools
Article Text:
‘Chennai shouldn’t alienate Delhi’: SC tells Tamil Nadu to reconsider opposition to Navodaya schools

Tamil Nadu raises language concerns

Court stresses cooperative federalism

State raises financial concerns

Supreme Court refuses to recall land direction

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday directed the Tamil Nadu government to comply with its December 15, 2025 order to identify land in every district for establishing Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas, while urging the state and Centre to resolve their differences over the schools through dialogue.A bench of Justices BV Nagarathna and Augustine George Masih also questioned Tamil Nadu's opposition to the three-language policy followed by Navodaya schools and said the state should not view the establishment of the centrally funded institutions as a threat to its existing education system."You have to change your mindset, it can’t be that Hindi will not be taught in the soil of Tamil Nadu," Justice Nagarathna observed during the hearing.The bench also said the people in Chennai should not alienate those in Delhi while stressing the need for cooperative federalism."We are saying in addition to all the good things you’re doing in your State, having something in addition will not bring down your standards. Coming from Delhi, will not lower the standards of Chennai. People in Chennai should not alienate Delhi and vice versa," the Court said.The court granted Tamil Nadu three more months to identify suitable land in each district and directed representatives of the state and Central governments to hold further discussions on the policy for establishing the schools.The matter has been posted for December 14.The case relates to Tamil Nadu's challenge to a Madras High Court direction to establish Navodaya Vidyalayas in every district.Navodaya schools are centrally funded, co-educational residential schools run by the Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti under the Union Ministry of Education. Tamil Nadu has opposed their establishment, among other reasons, because the schools follow a three-language policy that includes Hindi, while the state follows a two-language policy.Senior Advocate Jaideep Gupta, appearing for Tamil Nadu, told the court that the state's objection was not to schools or the teaching of Hindi as such, but to the language policy associated with the Navodaya scheme."It is against the State policy. It supersedes Tamil. This kind of unification is not the purport of the Constitution. It is not a Central government school. It is a school run by a society. There is an adamancy that Hindi must predominate."Justice Nagarathna said the language issue could be discussed between the Centre and the state."If you want Tamil as a second language, it is a matter which can be considered," the Judge said, asking the state Secretary to speak to the corresponding Central government Secretary.Gupta said discussions had already taken place but the Centre had remained adamant about Hindi. He nevertheless agreed to another round of consultations.Tamil Nadu also argued that the judiciary could not compel a state to adopt an optional Central government policy through a mandamus.Gupta submitted that education is in the Concurrent List and that Tamil Nadu has constitutional authority to frame its own education policy. He also argued that the Navodaya scheme was not compulsory.Justice Nagarathna questioned the consequences of individual states refusing to accept Central policies."Education is in the Concurrent List. There has to be cooperative federalism. If each State says that I don't accept your policy, what will happen?" the Judge asked.The bench said Tamil Nadu could continue running its own institutions and following its own syllabus, while Navodaya schools would provide an additional educational option.The court also rejected the argument that the establishment of Navodaya schools would lower Tamil Nadu's educational standards."We are not alienating you and we are not alienating them. Some more type of schools come in your state also which will only enhance the high standard which we are aware of. This is not going to lower your standards. If Navodaya schools were going to lower the standard of education in Tamil Nadu we would have said that irrespective of what you would have said. That is not the case here. It will provide more opportunity," Justice Nagarathna told Gupta."Ultimately everybody must work together," Justice Nagarathna said.Tamil Nadu also raised financial concerns, submitting that the Centre had promised to release Rs 5,000 crore for education but had not done so.Gupta argued that the state could not take on additional financial liabilities when funds under existing schemes had allegedly not been released.Additional Solicitor General KM Nataraj, appearing for the Centre, submitted that the state's primary requirement under the scheme was to provide land, while construction and other expenses would be borne by the Central government.Nataraj said the scheme was at an early stage and construction would take several years, during which the language-related differences could be addressed through discussions.Gupta, however, said around 30 acres of land would be required in each district and that identifying land before deciding whether to accept the policy would create difficulties.The bench clarified that it was not directing the state to acquire land immediately, but only to identify suitable land in its government plan.The Supreme Court had in December 2025 directed Tamil Nadu to identify land required for establishing Navodaya Vidyalayas in every district within six weeks. The state subsequently sought recall of the order.On Thursday, the bench declined to recall the direction and instead granted the state three months to comply.In its order, the bench recorded that Tamil Nadu had cited the change in government and lack of material progress in discussions with the Centre as reasons for non-compliance."Be that as it may, we direct the petitioner to comply with our order of 15.12.2025 in so far as identification of the land necessary to establish the school in each district," the order stated.The bench also directed the Centre and Tamil Nadu to continue discussions on the policy while the state works on identifying the land.Advocates G Priyadarshini and Rahul Shyam Bhandari, appearing for Kumari Maha Sabha, the petitioner before the High Court, argued that Tamil Nadu could not deny students access to free education through Navodaya schools."The Court should not get into this debate," Gupta said during the hearing.Justice Nagarathna responded: "That perception that you are surrendering to the central govt should not be there."
Article Summary: Supreme court tells tamil nadu to comply with its december 15, 2025 order to identify land in every district for jawahar navodaya vidyalayas. Justices bv nagarathna and augustine george masih also questioned tamil nadu's opposition to the three-language policy.

Article Title: Kashmir cracks walnut success code, turns to medium-sized, grafted trees
Article Text:
A street vendor sells walnuts on the occasion of the Sayar festival, in Mandi on Wednesday. (ANI Photo)

KOKERNAG: In Gohan village, around 100km south of Srinagar, Shabir Ahmad was among many harvesting walnuts from a towering tree. The work has become increasingly difficult. “My back aches now,” Ahmad said. J&K produces 3.5 lakh tonnes of walnuts annually, around 90% of the country’s total output.Like other villagers, Ahmad had no safety gear and he was proud of it. “We have been doing it for centuries,” said Ahmad, also a clerk at a local court. However, the bravado doesn’t help in harvesting seasons. Dr. Mohd Yaqoob Bhat, a surgeon at Paras Hospital in Srinagar, said Valley healthcare units treat dozens of patients each year after falls from walnut trees, some with serious spinal injuries. “There is no mechanism to address the issue,” Bhat said.Ahmad’s younger brother sold one walnut for one rupee and no two fruits are similar. For generations, Kashmir’s walnut trees have been grown from seeds. J&K and Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology (SKUAST) are now promoting medium-sized, grafted walnut trees to bring greater uniformity and help the produce compete globally amid competition from soft-shelled varieties grown in California and Chile.The initiative aims to replace scattered plantations with organised orchards of known varieties, allowing farmers to grow more trees in the same area and produce walnuts more consistent in size and color.J&K has about 80,000 hectares under walnut cultivation, most of it made up of seedling-origin trees. “When someone plants a walnut seed in the ground, whatever grows becomes a tree. Every tree is a variety of its own,” Ashfaq A. Pandit, professor and head of fruit science at SKUAST, said. This natural variation, once considered an advantage, has become a challenge in the modern market where buyers seek consistent produce.Traditional walnut trees can take about 15 years to bear fruit without using pesticides. Unlike traditional seedling-origin trees, grafted walnuts belong to known varieties.Imtiyaz Ahmad Lone, professor and head of SKUAST’s Walnut Research Centre, said the university released new walnut cultivars and grafting-based cultivation had spread over nearly 90,000 hectares despite lack of subsidies.Farmers argued, however, that the grafted varieties are no match for the traditional Kashmiri walnut. “It is no match in taste. The new varieties are brittle, tasteless. They are a no-show,” Mohammad Sultan, a Pulwama farmer in the business for 50 years, said.Researchers differed. Lone pointed out that grafted trees have early bearing, give faster returns as orchards and nut quality are uniform. “They have higher productivity and better export potential. There is a gradual opportunity to replace unproductive seedling trees,” he said.The transition has impacted walnut woodcraft industries. Walnut trees cannot be cut in J&K without govt permission. The matter was debated in the assembly in March when CM Omar Abdullah opposed a bill allowing landowners to cut walnut trees on private property. Omar defended the restrictions, saying the law served a broader purpose of conserving walnut and chinar trees.
Article Summary: J&k produces 3.5 lakh tonnes of walnuts annually, around 90% of the country’s total output. J&k and sher-e-kashmir university of agricultural sciences and technology (skuast) are promoting medium-sized, grafted walnut trees.

Vijay's team announced the cancellation over a loudspeaker, citing the lack of police permission on safety grounds.“For public safety concerns, we are calling off the programme because we don't have permission due to safety concerns,” a member of the chief minister's team said.Hours after the cancellation of the event, TVK's IT wing said in a social media post on X urged fans to refrain from waiting at the entrance of the hotel or making any attempts to meet him."We would be filled with love and heartfelt enthusiasm to meet the Tamil Nadu chief minister Thiru C Joseph Vijay. Article Title: Flowers at 10,600ft: World’s highest twin fields unveiled in Leh
Article Text:
Spread across 40 acres at Choglamsar and Stakna, the gardens house more than 25 lakh high-value flowers,

JAMMU/SRINAGAR: On Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s 76th birthday, Ladakh Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena inaugurated the world’s highest and India’s largest twin flower fields in Leh, at an altitude of 10,600ft, on Thursday as part of the administration’s efforts to diversify agriculture, build skills and create new livelihood opportunities in the Union Territory.Spread across 40 acres at Choglamsar and Stakna, the gardens house more than 25 lakh high-value flowers, including 24 lakh Lilium and 1 lakh Gladiolus. The Choglamsar field was developed in just two months, with plantation beginning on July 16 and the first blooms appearing in the first week of Sept. At Stakna, nearly 1.4 lakh lilies were planted in Aug, with the first blooms expected by Oct-end.Saxena said the initiative was the first experiment of its size and nature at such a high altitude in Leh, adding that its successful execution could pave the way for replication elsewhere in Ladakh. The gardens will open to the public on Sept 18, with an entry fee of Rs 25 for adults and Rs 10 for children, officials said.Floriculture, as a high-value agricultural activity, can complement traditional farming, increase cultivators’ incomes and create opportunities for employment and entrepreneurship, the LG said. The Choglamsar flower park will serve as a training, demonstration and model floriculture centre for farmers and youth, where Lilium, Gladiolus, Tulips and other ornamental flowers will be cultivated for national and international markets.“The facility will provide exposure to modern cultivation techniques, scientific farming practices and improved post-harvest management, enabling farmers to acquire the knowledge and skills required to take up floriculture at farm and village levels,” Saxena said. “Besides functioning as a recreational and educational space for residents and tourists, it will create an ecosystem where not only flowers, but also knowledge, skills and enterprises can grow,” he added.
Article Summary: Spread across 40 acres at choglamsar and stakna, the gardens house more than 25 lakh high-value flowers. The gardens will open to the public on sept 18, with an entry fee of rs 25 for adults and rs 10 for children.

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Thursday barred both rival Trinamool Congress (TMC) factions from using the party's name and reserved election symbol in the upcoming West Bengal Assembly bypolls, according to an interim order.The decision comes ahead of the October 6 bypolls in Nandigram and Rejinagar, where factions led by Mamata Banerjee and Ritabrata Banerjee had fielded candidates while staking claim to the TMC identity and its twin-flowers-on-grass symbol.The poll panel has been hearing competing claims from the two factions over control of the party, its name and election symbol. Both sides have submitted documents and appeared before the Commission during the proceedings.The dispute reached the Election Commission in July after the rival factions staked competing claims to control of the TMC. The Commission subsequently sought responses on issues including organisational control, authorised signatories, party assets, name and election symbol.The issue gained urgency after the EC announced the Nandigram and Rejinagar bypolls for October 6. With nominations closing on September 16, the Commission faced a deadline to determine how the rival factions would contest the elections.The Commission held separate meetings with representatives of both factions on September 12.The Mamata faction was represented by Derek O'Brien, Kalyan Banerjee, Sagarika Ghose, Saket Gokhale and advocate Abhinav Singh. The Ritabrata faction was represented by Ritabrata Banerjee, Akhruzzaman, Arup Roy, Chandrima Bhattacharya and Riju Datt.Both sides maintained that they represented the legitimate TMC and sought recognition of their claim to the party name and symbol.The Mamata faction argued that Banerjee remained the party chairperson and that the national working committee was still within its five-year term.The rival faction contended that the party constitution provided for a three-year term, which it said had ended in February 2025.On September 13, the EC sought final submissions from both factions by 3 pm on September 16, the nomination deadline for the two bypolls. The Commission indicated that another hearing could be held on September 17.At the time, the Mamata faction said that in the absence of an interim order, it would contest using the original TMC symbol. The Ritabrata faction maintained that the EC alone could decide which side was entitled to use the party name and symbol.On September 15, TOI reported that the Commission was likely to issue an interim ruling on September 17. The EC subsequently scheduled another hearing with both factions on Thursday.
Article Summary: Tmc vs tmc: ec bars both factions from using party symbol, name in bengal bypolls. Decision comes ahead of the october 6 by polls in nandigram and rejinagar. Factions led by mamata banerjee and ritabratabanerjee had fielded candidates while staking claim to the tmc identity.

NEW DELHI: Nudged by Supreme Court to reduce the cut-off percentile for admission to super specialty medical courses to fill around 2,000 vacant seats, Centre Thursday told the court that the qualifying percentile for NEET-SS may go from the existing 50th to 30th for the proposed special stray vacancy round, to be conducted soon, reports Amit Anand Choudhary.SC last week asked govt to reconsider its decision not to reduce the cut-off percentile in order to ensure seats were not wasted. Govt filed a two-page note before a bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe and said "the matter has since been reconsidered in consultation with stakeholders concerned"."In order to ensure available super specialty seats do not remain vacant and that the available training capacity is optimally utilised, it has been decided that the qualifying percentile for NEET-SS may be reduced from existing 50th percentile to 30th percentile for the purpose of proposed special stray vacancy round," govt said.It, however, told SC those students who had already taken admission would not be allowed to participate in the special stray vacancy round. It proposed the round "be conducted strictly in accordance with the existing principles or rules applicable to a stray vacancy round, with no provision for upgradation of candidates who are already holding/joined a seat", govt said.After the second round of NEET-SS counselling, 1,857 super specialty seats - including 1,094 DM/MCh seats and 763 DNB-SS seats - were vacant. A substantial number of these pertain to highly specialised medical and surgical disciplines.
Article Summary: Sc last week asked govt to reconsider its decision not to reduce the cut-off percentile. Centre thursday told the court that the qualifying percentile for neet-ss may go from the existing 50th to 30th for the proposed special stray vacancy round, to be conducted soon.

Article Title: SC raps CBSE for refusing to exempt Class VI from 3-language policy this year
Article Text:
CBSE had decided to enforce the three-language policy for all classes from Class VI to X

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday rapped CBSE for being stubborn in its decision to enforce the three-language policy from this year for Class VI students and forced it to reconsider the decision with a clear mandate, camouflaged as a suggestion, to enforce it from next academic year.CBSE had decided to enforce the three-language policy for all classes from Class VI to X, in which the students were to choose three languages of which two must be indigenous. On SC's request, it reconsidered and agreed to enforce it from Class VI onwards from this year while students in Class VII to X were to be governed by the old policy.SC had asked CBSE to reconsider exempting students of Class VI this year.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana is dealing with a bunch of petitions challenging the threelanguage policy, including highlighting the inadequacy of textbooks, indigenous subject teachers and infrastructure.When additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati told the bench that CBSE is disinclined to exempt Class VI this year and argued, “Let the Class VI students start this year as they would have three more years before appearing in Class X board examination,” the bench said, “It is your cohort who decided that it must be enforced from Class VI without considering the comfort of the Class VI students upon whom you sprung a surprise.“When the notification for enforcing the policy came, the student was already in Class VI. Go back and reconsider. Anyway, the academic year will come to an end in a few months. You enforce it for Class VI students from the 2027-28 academic year,” it said.Bhati agreed to take back the decision for reconsideration. The bench said exempting Class VI students from the policy this year would be without prejudice to CBSE’s right to defend the policy. “The exemption is purely from the aspect of logistics and balance of convenience,” it said.SC said, “There are more contentious issues on what can be considered an indigenous language (Petitioners say English should be considered as one while Centre objects to it) which we will decide later.”It added, “There must be some degree of comfort for the students. Those who would be coming to Class VI next year would know in advance that they must choose languages as per the three-language policy.You can also make it optional for Class VI students with adequate incentives so those who want to conform to the policy can choose to do so.” SC posted the matter for further hearing on Wednesday.
Article Summary: Cbse had decided to enforce the three-language policy for all classes from class vi to x. sc had asked cbse to reconsider exempting students of class vi this year. On sc's request, it reconsidered and agreed to enforce it from this year while students in class vii to x were to be governed by old policy.

Article Title: SC takes exception to 31 unnatural deaths in Manipur relief camps
Article Text:
The bench directed the state chief secretary to submit what remedial measures would be taken to prevent such incidents

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday took strong exception to 31 unnatural deaths in Manipur's relief camps - set up after the eruption of Kuki-Meitei ethnic clashes in 2023 to shelter internally displaced persons (IDPs) - including one due to sexual assault.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked the state govt to file an affidavit giving details of the causes of death as ascertained through postmortem reports and the investigations to identify the culprits. It also questioned the state for giving a meagre Rs 30,000 as compensation to the next of kin even though the state had paid Rs 4 lakh-5 lakh to relatives of victims of the ethnic clashes.This order was passed after perusing Justice Gita Mittal Committee's report. Placed before the court by senior advocate Vibha D Makhija, it cited a TOI report of June 7 which published a news report on 731 deaths, including 25 unnatural deaths, in relief camps as disclosed by the state home department. TOI had also reported that 43,000 IDPs were residing in various relief camps.Makhija said when the committee sought details of the deaths, the state initially provided sketchy statistics.Only after prodding did govt provide the required information. Jiribam and Churachandpur relief camps recorded nine unnatural deaths each; six were reported in Bishnupur, four in Imphal West, two in Imphal East and one in Kakching.The bench directed the state chief secretary to submit what remedial measures would be taken to prevent such incidents. It also asked the state to detail the steps taken to expedite investigations into the FIRs.Justice Mittal Committee informed the court that the mother of the sexual assault victim in Churachandpur relief camp was given Rs 2.5 lakh as compensation but in most cases, the next of kin got only Rs 30,000. In Kangpokpi relief camp, where 128 IDPs died natural deaths, no compensation was paid to their kin, it said.
Article Summary: The bench of chief justice surya kant and justices joymalya bagchi and v mohana asked the state govt to file an affidavit. It also questioned the state for giving a meagre rs 30,000 as compensation to the next of kin even though the state had paid rs 4 lakh-5 lakh to relatives of victims of the ethnic clashes.

Article Title: Tamil Nadu must change mindset, allow Hindi in schools: SC
Article Text:
People in Chennai should not alienate Delhi and vice versa, the court said

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday told Tamil Nadu govt that it needed to change its mindset towards teaching Hindi in schools and should thrash out issues with Centre on setting up Navodaya Vidyalayas in every district.As Vijay-led TN govt took the same stand taken by the previous DMK govt, a bench of Justices B V Nagarathna and A G Masih said individual states could not act like countries. "You have to change your mindset, it can't be that Hindi will not be taught on the soil of TN," the bench said.TN has been opposing the setting up of these schools as they follow a three-language policy, including Hindi, which is against the state's two-language policy."We are saying in addition to all the good things you're doing in your state, having something in addition will not bring down your standards... People in Chennai should not alienate Delhi and vice versa," SC said.Senior advocate Jaideep Gupta, appearing for the state, submitted it was against the federal structure to impose Centre's decision on a state. "It is against the state policy. It supersedes Tamil. This kind of unification is not the purport of Constitution.It is not a central govt school. It is a school run by a society. There is an adamancy that Hindi must predominate," he said.Gupta submitted that cooperative federalism would never work in only one direction and such a policy should not be enforced by the court.The bench asked the state to comply with its order and posted the case for further hearing in Dec. SC had last Dec directed TN to identify land required for establishing Navodaya Vidyalayas in each district within six weeks."We are not asking you to acquire land. We are only asking you to identify it... There is a need for dialogue. You can't say I won't accept a policy. Today it is education, tomorrow it will be something else. You have to relax this rigidity in your mind," SC said.The court was hearing TN's plea challenging a Madras HC judgement directing it to set up Navodaya Vidyalayas in every district. HC had ruled that Navodaya Vidyalayas did not violate Tamil Nadu Tamil Learning Act and the state's blanket refusal to set up such schools curtailed students' right to choose educational institutions.
Article Summary: Supreme court tells tamil nadu govt that it needs to change its mindset towards teaching hindi in schools. Justices b v nagarathna and a g masih said individual states could not act like countries.tn has been opposing the setting up of these schools as they follow a three-language policy, including hindi.

Article Title: EC accepts TMC split, freezes name, symbol in interim order
Article Text:
EC barred both factions from using party symbol, name in Bengal bypolls

NEW DELHI: Acknowledging the split in All India Trinamool Congress (AITC) — with one faction led by Mamata Banerjee and the other by Arup Roy — the Election Commission on Thursday froze its reserved “flowers and grass” poll symbol until final settlement of the intra-party dispute by the commission.For the purpose of the October 6 assembly bypolls in Rejinagar and Nandigram — where both factions have fielded separate candidates under TMC name — the EC in its interim ruling said both the groups may pick a different party name, including which may have linkage with parent party name AITC, and also choose their respective poll symbol from the list of free symbols notified by the poll panel.The two groups have been asked to furnish to EC by Friday 11 am, three options for names by which they may be recognised by the commission, as well as the symbols to be allotted to the candidates set up by them. The chosen names and symbols may be stated in order of preference, for final approval by EC. Once the new party name and symbol are allotted to the two factions, the concerned returning officers will complete the scrutiny of nominations for the two bypolls.EC, in its interim ruling on Thursday, opined after due consideration of submissions made by both Mamata and Arup Roy factions, that there exist two rival groups in AITC, with each claiming to be the “real” party.“Therefore the matter requires a substantive determination by threcommission under Para 15 of the Election Symbols (Reservation & Allotment) Order 1968,” it noted.In order to "place the rival groups on an even keel" and based on past precedents, EC ordered that neither of the two factions shall be permitted to use the AITC name or its “flowers and grass” symbol until termination of the dispute under the Symbols Order.EC’s interim ruling places on record full chronology or the intra-party dispute as well as the submissions made by the two groups — through Mamata Bannerjee and Ritabrata Banerjee and others — since June 22, 2026. The basic contention rests on the Ritabrata questioning the constitutional mandate and authority of the AITC national working committee (NWC) to make key appointments in the party on June 5, 2026. Ritabrata argued that tenure of NWC had expired on 11.02.2025, and that it was his group that later reconstituted NWC on June 22, 2026 with Arup Roy as chairperson. On July 6, Mamata said the claims of rival group were fundamentally flawed and illegal and contrary to the party constitution, which gave NCW a five-year tenure ending in 2027.Derek O Brien, it was underlined, had submitted to EC on 07.03.2026 the amended party Constitution for uploading on the commission website.Both sides have since made several submissions to the EC, both in writing and in person, in support of their claims and countering the claims of the rival group to being the real party. The final set of submissions were made by the Arup Roy faction on Sept 16. Both the factions finally met EC in person on Friday, hours before the commission issued the interim ruling freezing the AITC symbol.The interim order coincided with the scheduled date for scrutiny of nominations. As per rules, if necessitated by circumstances that include a dispute over candidates claiming to be fielded by the same party, the returning officer can delay scrutiny of nominations until almost 11 AM on the scheduled day for withdrawal of candidatures.The commission decides a symbol dispute arising from a split in the party, using its quasi-judicial powers. The rival factions are represented before the EC by senior lawyers who argue the case in in-person hearings scheduled by the commission. Both sides are given an opportunity to present their arguments endorsing their claim over the party name and symbol and to also counter the arguments by the rival side. The hearings in a symbol row often span over months.The commission, after hearing both sides and examining their claims and counter-claims, gives a well-reasoned order recognising one of the factions as the “real" party entitled to use its reserved symbol.Over the years, the EC has decided symbol disputes in parties like the Shiv Sena, NCP, AIADMK, Samajwadi Party, Lok Janshakti Party, etc. In all these cases, the final verdict was preceded by an interim order freezing the reserved symbol of these parties.
Article Summary: Ec barred both factions from using party symbol, name in bengal bypolls on october 6. One faction led by mamata banerjee and the other by arup roy. Both factions have fielded separate candidates under tmc name. Ec decides a symbol dispute arising from a split in the party, using its quasi-judicial powers.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday took a serious view of a large number of anonymous complaints received by it against judges, amici curiae and counsel after SC turned up the heat on several realtors and builders for misusing subvention schemes, duping homebuyers, delaying projects and refusing to refund the money invested."We will direct a CBI inquiry into these complaints to find out who are behind it," said a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, after additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati handed over the CBI status report on its investigations into builders who had misused subvention schemes in collusion with bank officials, resulting in homebuyers paying EMIs without any hope of getting their dream homes even after waiting for decades.CJI Kant asked, "In these matters, who are the counsel representing the builders? You (builders) have started sending anonymous complaints to us? You people do not know what kind of stubborn people we are."Turning to Bhati, the CJI said on the next hearing date, "we will give you another set of complaints. You inquire into them and find out who the people responsible for writing these are. Most of them will be builders, we assume, and, of course, some counsel who have ill-advised them"."We will catch hold of them. Do you think we will get cowed down by this? We will direct CBI to register an FIR and investigate them. We will take it to the logical conclusion," the bench said.In April last year, SC had ordered a CBI investigation into the abuse of subvention agreements by builders and banks. At the last hearing, Bhati had informed SC that CBI had registered 50 FIRs and completed probes in 18 of them, filing 17 chargesheets and a closure report before competent courts.She said several bank officials were found to have been in collusion with the builders and were named among the accused in the chargesheets, and the agency had invoked provisions of Prevention of Corruption Act against them. CBI has sought sanctions for prosecuting bank officials from State Bank of India, Bank of India, Uco Bank, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank.SC had directed banks to expeditiously grant sanction for prosecution and said failure to do so would warrant submission of an explanation before the court.SC had also directed CBI to conduct a thorough investigation into allegations of misrepresentation and other irregularities by entities known as "Ozone group in Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu; Vivansaa in Bengaluru; Rudra Buildwell Pvt Ltd in Greater Noida; and Omaxe group in Chandigarh". It had sought a separate probe status report in this regard.
Article Summary: Supreme court thursday took a serious view of a large number of anonymous complaints received by it against judges, amici curiae and counsel. Sc turned up the heat on several realtors and builders for misusing subvention schemes, duping homebuyers and delaying projects.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday allowed Dara Singh to amend his petition to challenge Odisha govt's rejection of his remission plea after the state informed the court about its decision. It agreed to hear his amended petition after three weeks.A bench of Justices Manoj Misra and Vijay Bishnoi allowed Singh's lawyer to challenge the order passed by Odisha by amending the petition within two weeks.Singh, incarcerated for 26 years, was sentenced to death by a trial court in 2003 for the murder of Australian missionary Graham Staines and his two sons. In 2005, Odisha HC commuted the death penalty to life imprisonment, which was confirmed by SC in 2011. Singh was part of a mob which on Jan 22, 1999, had set fire to Staines's vehicle in which he and his sons, Philip (10) and Timothy (6), were sleeping.SC had pulled up Odisha govt over its indecisiveness on taking a call on the remission plea and had set it a deadline of Sept 17. "You cannot keep it lingering like this. Accept or reject it. You cannot avoid taking decision," the bench had said.

NEW DELHI: As Congress members of Parliament's standing committee on finance sought to dissociate themselves from the panel's support for MDR on UPI transactions, its chairperson, Bhartruhari Mahtab, questioned their claim, noting their presence in the meeting and being party to the report were matters of record."It is all on the record. The MPs were present and participated in the discussion. The report was read out to them and their approval taken before it was adopted and submitted to Speaker Om Birla on the issue of demand for grants," Mahtab, a parliamentarian of seven Lok Sabha terms, said.He said the record showed that three opposition MPs - TMC's Saugata Roy and Congress's Manish Tewari and Pramod Tiwari - were part of the deliberations, which made the recommendations to levy merchant discount rate (MDR). The report was tabled in LS on March 12.The committee had backed the introduction of MDR, saying a viable revenue mechanism needed to be found to ensure financial sustainability of the UPI system. It noted, "While UPI is expected to process up to 150 billion transactions per month and add 600 million new users, the current govt incentive covers merely 11% of industry's actual costs and 14% of potential MDR collections, creating a structural funding gap impacting long-term infrastructure investment.With Congress brass flaying govt for introducing MDR, some of its MPs rubbished the contention that they had supported the levy, calling it a "pathetic" attempt by BJP to divert attention from the backlash to the "UPI tax".Deputy leader of the opposition in LS Gaurav Gogoi and Manish Tewari claimed the standing committee did not discuss the "UPI tax" that govt has announced, as the department of finance did not have any specific proposal on the issue when they last met the panel. Gogoi said while questions were raised on the need for MDR, govt representatives did not have satisfactory answers.Agreeing with Gogoi, Tewari accused govt of misusing the privileged proceedings of the standing committee to make political points. "No specific proposal qua the recent MDR to be levied on UPI transactions from Oct 15 was ever brought before the committee on finance - rate, quantum, amount of fee to be charged, ceiling and exemption slabs, etc," he said.Instead, Tewari said, concerns were raised by the committee members about the need and efficacy of MDR over the course of various sittings of the committee.When asked about their denial, Mahtab, a BJP MP, maintained this was a matter of record and could be verified from the LS secretariat.Govt sources also said the final report is shared with all members of a committee before it is adopted, and an MP can submit a dissent if s/he does not agree with any of the recommendations. This report was adopted unanimously, they stressed.
Article Summary: Congress members of parliament's standing committee on finance sought to dissociate themselves from the panel's support for mdr on upi transactions. The committee's chairperson, bhartruhari mahtab, questioned their claim, noting their presence in the meeting and being party to the report were matters of record.
